YMCA YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTERS (1922)
New York: Association Press. Internet Archive: ymcayearbookoffi01youn

NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED. The full djvu text (1,508,916 bytes) was downloaded and searched.
"Kanawana" occurs ZERO times — as in all nine volumes of this series now held. It rosters staff,
not programmes.

WHY THIS VOLUME. p_433 named it next because 1922 is the season Lemuel P. Ereaux directed the camp
and Hay Finlay ran its senior section.


THE YMCA OF MONTREAL, 1922
--------------------------

    Montreal, 127 Drummond St.
      President, GERALD W. BIRKS
      Gen. Secy., J. W. Beaton

      Secy., W. J. HOLLIDAY


FIVE THINGS
-----------

**W. J. HOLLIDAY IS STILL THERE, AND HE IS RUNNING A BRANCH.** `directors-index.md` says of the man
who opened Kanawana: "How far past 1910 he continued is not stated." He is **Secretary of the North
Branch at 2300 Park Avenue in 1922**. His documented Montreal career now runs **1906 to 1922 at
least**: Assistant Secretary 1906, Boys' Work Director 1907-08, camp director 1910-12?, branch
secretary by 1922.

**HAY FINLAY IS GONE**, and the timing is exact. He is "Asst. Physical, Hay Finlay" at Central in
the 1921 volume; Central's assistant physicals in 1922 are O. S. McCutcheon and George F. Harris.
Kanawana's 1922 brochure calls him "**ex**-Central YMCA Boys' Physical Director, then at McGill
Physical Education". The roster puts his departure between the two volumes — the same season he ran
the camp's senior section.

**MacKINNON AND BRANDON BOTH MOVED.** John G. MacKinnon was Industrial Secretary in 1921 and is at
**Côte St. Paul** in 1922; Grant D. Brandon was Community Secretary in 1921 and is at **Verdun**.
Both are branch or district postings, which is what a boys'-work man's career does after the camp
seasons this project records for them (MacKinnon 1916-19, Brandon 1918 and 1921).

**THE PRESIDENT CHANGED**: A. O. Dawson in 1921, GERALD W. BIRKS in 1922.

**D. A. BUDGE, TO THE MONTH.** The volume carries a continent-wide "LIST OF SECRETARIES ENTERING
ASSOCIATION SERVICE BEFORE JAN. 1, 1893, AND STILL EMPLOYED APRIL, 1922. (In a few cases service has
not been continuous)." Its fifth line reads:

    Mar. 1874    D. A. Budge, Consulting Sec, Montreal

Forty-eight years, and only four men on the whole continent ahead of him — Robert Weidensall
(Oct. 1868), Richard C. Morse (Dec. 1869), Isaac G. Jenkins (April 1871) and H. S. Ninde (July
1872). The general secretary who presided over the camp's founding entered YMCA service in **March
1874**.


AND ONE OUTSIDE MONTREAL
------------------------
Under ONTARIO AND QUEBEC TERRITORY, 86 Adelaide St. E., Toronto:

    tHarry Ballantyne   Territorial Secretary
    T. D. PATTON        Assistant Territorial Secretary
    Percival J. Lee     Assistant Territorial Secretary
    William R. Cook     Boys' Work Secretary
    A. S. Hopper        Financial Secretary

`t-duncan-patton.md` summarises his career as "Territorial Secretary at Toronto (1922-26)". The 1922
roster has him as **Assistant** Territorial Secretary, under Harry Ballantyne. Not a contradiction —
he may have been promoted inside that span — but the article's phrasing compresses an arrival into a
tenure, and the roster is the more precise witness for 1922.


NOT FOUND
---------
The volume's *Alphabetical List of Employed Officers* begins at scan line 18262, and W. J. Holliday
does not appear in it under that spelling; only five occurrences of "Holliday" exist in the whole
file and four are the Pennsylvania town of Hollidaysburg. Either the OCR has mangled his index line
or he is listed under a variant. The roster entry above is not in doubt.
